new.title: How Ipv4Addr::new works
new.description: An IPv4 address from its four numbers.

from_str.title: How parse works for Ipv4Addr
from_str.description: Parses text like "10.0.0.1" into an address.

slides.caption: Each part must be 0–255, with exactly four parts.

ipaddr-from_str.title: How parse works for IpAddr
ipaddr-from_str.description: Parses either an IPv4 or an IPv6 address.

slides.caption: The text decides which variant you get.
Match on IpAddr::V4 / V6 to handle each.
Host names like "localhost:80" need ToSocketAddrs instead.

octets.title: How Ipv4Addr::octets works
octets.description: The four bytes of the address.

to_bits.title: How Ipv4Addr::to_bits works
to_bits.description: The address as a single u32.

slides.caption: The highest byte is the first part.
Traffic to loopback never leaves the computer.

is_private.title: How Ipv4Addr::is_private works
is_private.description: true for home and office network ranges (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x).

slides.caption: These addresses are only valid inside a local network.
Binding to 0.0.0.0 listens on every network interface.
Packets to it reach every machine on the local network.
Multicast sends to a group of listeners.
Used by service discovery like mDNS.
A computer picks one when it cannot get an address.
Often a sign of network trouble.

is_documentation.title: How Ipv4Addr::is_documentation works
is_documentation.description: true for ranges reserved for examples (e.g. 192.0.2.x).

slides.caption: Use these in examples so nobody's real address is shown.

is_ipv4.title: How IpAddr::is_ipv4 works
is_ipv4.description: true if the address is an IPv4 one.

is_ipv6.title: How IpAddr::is_ipv6 works
is_ipv6.description: true if the address is an IPv6 one.

slides.caption: Match on IpAddr::V6(v6) to use its methods.
Allow admin pages only from loopback.

ipaddr-is_multicast.title: How IpAddr::is_multicast works
ipaddr-is_multicast.description: true for multicast addresses of either family.

slides.caption: Each family has its own multicast range.

to_canonical.title: How IpAddr::to_canonical works
to_canonical.description: Turns an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address back into plain IPv4.

slides.caption: Dual-stack servers often see IPv4 clients in this IPv6 form.
Normalise before comparing or logging addresses.

ipv6-new.title: How Ipv6Addr::new works
ipv6-new.description: An IPv6 address from its eight 16-bit groups.

slides.caption: Runs of zero groups are shortened to :: when printed.

ipv6-from_str.title: How parse works for Ipv6Addr
ipv6-from_str.description: Parses text like "fe80::1" into an address.

slides.caption: Brackets are only for socket addresses: "[::1]:80".

segments.title: How Ipv6Addr::segments works
segments.description: The eight 16-bit groups of the address.

slides.caption: The :: expands to the missing zero groups.
The lowest bits are the last group.
Unlike IPv4, there is a single loopback address.
Binding to :: listens on every IPv6 interface.

ipv6-is_multicast.title: How Ipv6Addr::is_multicast works
ipv6-is_multicast.description: true for addresses starting with ff.

slides.caption: ff02::1 means "all nodes on this link".

is_unique_local.title: How Ipv6Addr::is_unique_local works
is_unique_local.description: true for fc00::/7, the IPv6 equivalent of private addresses.

slides.caption: Used inside companies and home labs.

is_unicast_link_local.title: How Ipv6Addr::is_unicast_link_local works
is_unicast_link_local.description: true for fe80::/10, valid only on the local link.

slides.caption: Automatically assigned; never routed beyond the link.
Often needs a scope id (%eth0) to use.

to_ipv4_mapped.title: How Ipv6Addr::to_ipv4_mapped works
to_ipv4_mapped.description: The IPv4 address inside an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address.

ipv6-to_canonical.title: How Ipv6Addr::to_canonical works
ipv6-to_canonical.description: An IpAddr: V4 if the address is IPv4-mapped, otherwise V6.

slides.caption: Handy for logging client addresses on dual-stack servers.

socketaddr-new.title: How SocketAddr::new works
socketaddr-new.description: An IP address plus a port.

ip.title: How SocketAddr::ip works
ip.description: The IP part of a socket address.

slides.caption: Port 0 asks the OS to pick a free one.

set_ip.title: How SocketAddr::set_ip works
set_ip.description: Changes the IP address, keeping the port.

slides.caption: May even switch between IPv4 and IPv6.

socketaddr-is_ipv4.title: How SocketAddr::is_ipv4 works
socketaddr-is_ipv4.description: true if the address part is IPv4.

socketaddr-is_ipv6.title: How SocketAddr::is_ipv6 works
socketaddr-is_ipv6.description: true if the address part is IPv6.

slides.caption: IPv6 socket addresses are written in brackets.
Match on SocketAddr::V6 for flowinfo and scope id.

socketaddr_v4-new.title: How SocketAddrV4::new works
socketaddr_v4-new.description: An IPv4 address plus a port.

slides.caption: The specific type when you know it is IPv4.
Returns a reference to the address.

socketaddr_v4-port.title: How SocketAddrV4::port works
socketaddr_v4-port.description: The port of an IPv4 socket address.

slides.caption: The second half of the address.

socketaddr_v4-set_port.title: How SocketAddrV4::set_port works
socketaddr_v4-set_port.description: Changes the port of an IPv4 socket address.

socketaddr_v4-set_ip.title: How SocketAddrV4::set_ip works
socketaddr_v4-set_ip.description: Changes the IPv4 address, keeping the port.

socketaddr_v6-new.title: How SocketAddrV6::new works
socketaddr_v6-new.description: An IPv6 address, port, flow info and scope id.

slides.caption: A non-zero scope id prints as %n.
Without brackets the colons would be ambiguous.
Address in brackets, then the port.

scope_id.title: How SocketAddrV6::scope_id works
scope_id.description: Which network interface a link-local address belongs to.

slides.caption: Link-local addresses exist on every interface, so the scope picks one.

flowinfo.title: How SocketAddrV6::flowinfo works
flowinfo.description: The IPv6 flow label and traffic class field.

slides.caption: Routers may use it to keep packets of one flow together.

from_octets.title: How Ipv4Addr::from_octets works
from_octets.description: An IPv4 address from an array of four bytes.

slides.caption: Handy when the bytes come from a packet.

from_segments.title: How Ipv6Addr::from_segments works
from_segments.description: An IPv6 address from eight 16-bit groups.

slides.caption: Same as Ipv6Addr::new with an array.

socketaddr_v6-port.title: How SocketAddrV6::port works
socketaddr_v6-port.description: The port of an IPv6 socket address.

slides.caption: The second half of the address.

socketaddr_v6-set_ip.title: How SocketAddrV6::set_ip works
socketaddr_v6-set_ip.description: Changes the IPv6 address, keeping the port.

set_flowinfo.title: How SocketAddrV6::set_flowinfo works
set_flowinfo.description: Changes the IPv6 flow information field.

slides.caption: Routers may use it to group packets.

set_scope_id.title: How SocketAddrV6::set_scope_id works
set_scope_id.description: Sets the interface index for link-local addresses.
